chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

When a man slaughters and shaves, then everything from which iḥrām had forbidden him becomes lawful for him except women and perfume. Then when he visits the House, performs tawaf, and does saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, then everything from which iḥrām had forbidden him becomes lawful for him except women. Then when he performs the tawaf of women, then everything from which iḥrām had forbidden him becomes lawful for him except hunting.

key_terms.أَحَلَّ: became released from prohibition and lawful again
key_terms.الطِّيبَ: perfume or fragrance forbidden in iḥrām
key_terms.حَلَقَ: shaved the head as part of hajj rites
key_terms.طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ: the tawaf after which women become lawful

ai.seo_question: What becomes permissible for a pilgrim after slaughtering, shaving, tawaf, and tawaf al-nisāʾ in hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the sequence of what becomes permissible for a pilgrim after the rites of sacrifice, shaving, tawaf, saʿy, and tawaf al-nisāʾ. It sets out the legal stages of release from iḥrām restrictions during hajj, with women, perfume, and hunting each becoming permissible at different points.
